meta.title: Bengali Alphabet (Bangla script)
meta.subtitle: 69 letters, signs and conjuncts, as two cards each · 11 rules of reading
meta.desc: The Bengali script (Bangla lipi), and how it is read: 80 notes, 149 cards. The first deck of the Bengali collection. In the traditional order: the 11 vowels, each shown alone and as the sign it becomes after a consonant, written on ক (আ · কা); the 5 signs that sit on or beside a letter; the 32 consonants row by row and the 3 dotted letters (ড়, ঢ়, য়); the two joined letters every primer teaches (ক্ষ, জ্ঞ); the phala signs and reph (য-ফলা, র-ফলা, ব-ফলা, রেফ); and the 12 other conjuncts that stand in two or more of Bengali A1's words (ন্ত, ষ্ট, স্ত, ক্ত …). A letter is two cards, each with its own schedule: see the letter and recall its sound, or see the sound and recall the letter. Between the groups stand 11 rule cards, one card each: the vowel no sign writes, the vowel signs, the letters that sound alike (ই ঈ, উ ঊ, শ ষ স, জ য, ন ণ), the vowel æ that has no letter, the breathy consonants beside the plain ones, the two kinds of t and d, the headstroke, and how consonants join. WHERE EVERY STATEMENT COMES FROM: nothing on a card is this deck's own description. A letter's name in romanisation and in the International Phonetic Alphabet is a cell of the vowel or consonant table of Wikipedia's 'Bengali alphabet' (revision 1379877198, 2026-10-12); the English sound it is like is the 'English approximation' cell of every row of Wikipedia's 'Help:IPA/Bengali' (revision 1369348573, 2026-08-14) that lists the letter, with that page's own regional labels (American, Scottish, Indian); a sign's function is its row of the first page's table 'Diacritics and other symbols'; and each longer statement is a sentence of the first page, or a note of the second, quoted whole — a cut is marked […] — and signed beneath. A rule card's heading is the only text written for the deck. What a conjunct is made of is read off the letter itself. Those two pages do not say that the inherent vowel is usually silent at the end of a word, nor which side of its consonant each vowel sign is written on, so no card says either: the example words show both. Every example word is a card of the level decks, the first in the order they are dealt that shows the letter, with a speaker and Wiktionary's romanisation and pronunciation: the romanisation follows the SPELLING and the pronunciation gives the SOUND, and the symbols of the second are the ones this deck teaches. At Folio's default of ten new cards a day this deck takes 15 days. Sources. Wikipedia, 'Bengali alphabet' and 'Help:IPA/Bengali', at the revisions above (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example words, their romanisation, pronunciation and meanings: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

bn-rule.name: Bengali reading rule

fields.Name: অ
fields.Sound: ô /ɔ~o/ɔ · offo · story
fields.Says:
[…] represents the default inherent vowel for the entire Bengali script.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
The underlying form of অ is /ɔ/. It is raised to [o] in the following contexts: · if অ is in the first syllable and there are high vowels (e.g. ই /i/ and উ /u/) in the following syllable, e.g., অতি ôti [ˈot̪iˑ] 'much', বলছি bôlchi [ˈboltʃʰiˑ] '(I am) speaking' · if অ is the inherent vowel in a word-initial consonant cluster ending in rôphôla, e.g., প্রথম prôthôm [ˈpɾot̪ʰɔm] 'first' · if the next consonant cluster contains a yôphôla (which geminates the preceding consonant), e.g., অন্য ônyô [ˈonːoˑ] 'other', জন্য jônyô [ˈdʒɔnːoˑ] 'for'Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: অনেকonek/ɔnek/many

fields.Name: আ
fields.Sound: a /ɐ/a · Australian father, RP cut
fields.Example:
আচ্ছাaccha/at͡ʃʰːa/okay, well
নমস্কারnomoskar/nɔmoʃkaɾ/(Hinduism) a salutation; a greeting used for most purposes including hello, good morning/afternoon, and goodbye

fields.Name: ই
fields.Sound: i /i/i · beati̯ (semivowel) · happy
fields.Example:
ইচ্ছাiccha/it͡ʃʰːa/desire, wish, will
বিদায়bidaẏ/bid̪ae̯/goodbye

fields.Name: ঈ
fields.Example:
ঈশ্বরiśśor/iʃːɔɾ/God, Ishvara
কীki/ki/what

fields.Name: উ
fields.Sound: u /u/u · coolu̯ (semivowel) · toow (marginal consonant) · will
fields.Example:
উনিuni/uni/he, she
তুমিtumi/t̪umi/you (familiar: to a friend, a younger relative)

fields.Name: ঊ
fields.Example:
ঊর্ধ্বতনurddhoton/uɾd̪ʱːɔt̪on/upper, higher
শূন্যśunno/ʃunːo/zero

fields.Name: ঋ
fields.Says: […] does not actually represent a vowel phoneme in Bengali, but instead represents the consonant-vowel combination রি /ri/.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
ঋণrin/rin/debt
বৃহস্পতিবারbrihośpotibar/bɾiɦoʃpot̪ibaɾ/Thursday

fields.Name: এ
fields.Sound: e /e/æ · trape · Scottish may
fields.Says: Even though the near-open front unrounded vowel /æ/ is one of the seven main vowel sounds in the standard Bengali language, no distinct vowel symbol has been allotted for it in the script, though এ is used. /æ/ may also be transcribed in IPA and pronounced as an open-mid front unrounded vowel /ɛ/.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
এe/e/he, she, it
সেśe/ʃe/he, she

fields.Name: ঐ
fields.Example:
ঐতিহাসিকōitihaśik/oi̯t̪ihaʃik/historic, historical
তৈরিtōiri/t̪oi̯ɾi/made, wrought

fields.Name: ও
fields.Sound: o /o~w/o · storyo̯ (semivowel) · Similar to lookw (marginal consonant) · will
fields.Example:
ওō/o/he, she, it
ভালোbhalō/bʱalo/good

fields.Name: ঔ
fields.Example: দৌড়ানোdōuṛanō/d̪ou̯ɽano/to run

fields.Title: The vowel no sign writes
fields.Says:
An exception to the above system is the vowel /ɔ/, which has no vowel mark but is considered inherent in every consonant letter. To denote the absence of the inherent vowel /ɔ/ following a consonant, a diacritic known as the virama (হসন্ত hôsôntô) may be written underneath the consonant.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
The names of the letters are typically just the consonant sound plus the inherent vowel অ ô. Since the inherent vowel is assumed and not written, most letters' names look identical to the letter itself (e.g., the name of the letter ঘ is itself ghô, not gh).Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
কখনkokhon/kɔkʰon/when, what time
কতkoto/kɔt̪o/how much
ছয়choẏ/t͡ʃʰɔe̯/six

fields.Letter: কা কি কী কু কূ কৃ কে কৈ কো কৌ
fields.Title: A vowel after a consonant is a sign
fields.Says: When a vowel sound occurs syllable-initially or when it follows another vowel, it is written using a distinct letter. When a vowel sound follows a consonant (or a consonant cluster), it is written with a diacritic which, depending on the vowel, can appear above, below, before or after the consonant. These vowel marks cannot appear without a consonant and are called kar (কার 'vowel sign').Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
ঠিকṭhik/ʈʰik/right, proper, correct
আছেache/ɑt͡ʃʰe/to have; to possess
তোমরাtōmra/t̪omɹä/you (plural, familiar)

fields.Title: Two letters, one vowel
fields.Says: There are two graphemes for the vowel sound /i/, and two graphemes for the vowel sound /u/. The redundancy stems from the time when this script was used to write Sanskrit, which had contrastive short and long vowels. Bengali lost phonemic long vowels and merged short and long /i/ and /u/: ই (হ্রস্ব ই hrôsbô i 'short i') and ঈ (দীর্ঘ ঈ dirghô i 'long i') are both pronounced /i/; and উ (হ্রস্ব উ 'short u') and ঊ (দীর্ঘ ঊ 'long u') are both pronounced /u/ in modern Bengali.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
আমিami/ɑmi/I
কীভাবেkibhabe/kibʱabe/how (in what manner)
তুইtui/t̪ui̯/you (intimate: to a close friend, a child)
দূরdur/d̪uɾ/distance

fields.Title: A vowel with no letter of its own
fields.Says: Even though the near-open front unrounded vowel /æ/ is one of the seven main vowel sounds in standard Bengali, no distinct vowel symbol has been allotted for it in the script since there is no /æ/ sound in Sanskrit—the primary written language when the script was conceived.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
হ্যাঁhễ/hæ̃/yes
দেওয়াdeoẇa/d̪æo̯ɑ/to give
নেওয়াneōẇa/næo̯ɑ/to take

fields.Name: অনুস্বার
fields.Sound: অনুস্বার ônusshar ṅ /ŋ/ŋ · sing
fields.Says: Diacritic. Final velar nasal [ŋ]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: এবংebông[ˈe.bɔŋ]and

fields.Name: বিসর্গ
fields.Sound: বিসর্গ bisôrgô ḥ /h/ɦ · behindh · head
fields.Says: Diacritic. 1. Doubles the next consonant sound without the vowel (spelling feature) in দুঃখ duḥkhô [ˈd̪uɦkʰoˑ] > [ˈd̪uʔkʰoˑ] > [ˈd̪uk̚kʰoˑ] 'sorrow' 2. Final -ḥ examples: এঃ eḥ, উঃ uḥ 3. Silent in spellings like আন্তঃনগর antôḥnôgôr [ˈant̪ɔɦˌnoɡɔɾ] > [ˈant̪ɔˌnoɡɔɾ] 'intercity' […]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: দুঃখdukkho/d̪ukʰːo/sorrow, grief, pain, regret

fields.Name: চন্দ্রবিন্দু
fields.Sound: চন্দ্রবিন্দু côndrôbindu ◌̃ / ṃ /◌̃/◌̃ · nasal vowel ([ã], [õ], etc.)
fields.Says: Diacritic. Vowel nasalisationWikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: হ্যাঁhễ/hæ̃/yes

fields.Name: হসন্ত
fields.Says: Diacritic. Suppresses the inherent vowel [ɔ]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: ধন্যবাদdhonnobad/d̪ʱonːobad̪/thank you

fields.Name: খণ্ড ত
fields.Sound: খণ্ড ত khôndô tô t /t̪/t · get (dental), Indian think
fields.Says:
Special character. Final unaspirated dental [t̪]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
As the first member of a conjunct, or when at the end of a word and followed by no vowel, ত tô can appear as ৎ […]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: চমৎকারcomotkar/t͡ʃɔmɔt̪kaɾ/amazing

fields.Name: ক
fields.Example: করাkôra/kɔɾa/to do

fields.Name: খ
fields.Example: খাওয়াkhaōẇa/kʰao̯a/to eat

fields.Name: গ
fields.Example: গাড়িgaṛi/ɡaɽi/car

fields.Name: ঘ
fields.Example: ঘরghor/ɡʱɔɾ/a house, building, residence

fields.Name: ঙ
fields.Example: ভাঙাbhaṅa/bʱaŋa/broken, fractured, split

fields.Name: চ
fields.Example: চাওয়াcaōẇa/t͡ʃao̯a/to want

fields.Name: ছ
fields.Example: ছেলেchele/t͡ʃʰele/boy

fields.Name: জ
fields.Sound: jô /dʒɔ~dʑɔ/d͡ʒ · hedgez (marginal consonant) · zip
fields.Example: জানাjana/d͡ʒana/to know

fields.Name: ঝ
fields.Example: ঝোঁকাjhō̃ka/d͡ʒʰo.ka/to lean, to stoop

fields.Name: ঞ
fields.Says: Original sound for ঞ was /ɲɔ/ but in modern Bengali, it represents /ẽɔ/ and in consonant conjuncts is pronounced /nɔ/ same as ন.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: মিঞাmĩa/mi̯ã/(Islam) man, gentleman; sir

fields.Name: ট
fields.Sound: ṭô /ʈɔ/ʈ · American part
fields.Example: টাকাṭaka/ʈaka/(Bangladesh) taka (৳)

fields.Name: ঠ
fields.Sound: ṭhô /ʈʰɔ/ʈʰ · American partake
fields.Example: ঠান্ডাṭhanḍa/ʈʰanɖa/cold, cool, chilly

fields.Name: ড
fields.Sound: ḍô /ɖɔ/ɖ · American bird
fields.Example: ডাকাḍaka/ɖaka/to call, to call for

fields.Name: ঢ
fields.Sound: ḍhô /ɖʱɔ/ɖʱ · American birdhouse
fields.Example: ঢোকাḍhōka/ɖʱoka/to enter, to go into, to come into

fields.Name: ণ
fields.Sound: ṇô /nɔ/n · notɳ (marginal consonant) · American burn
fields.Says: The original sound for ণ was /ɳɔ/ but in modern Bengali it is almost always pronounced /nɔ/, the same as ন. An exception is in conjuncts with other retroflex letters, where the original sound for ণ can occasionally be found.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: কারণkaron/ka.ron/because

fields.Name: ত
fields.Sound: tô /t̪ɔ/t · get (dental), Indian think
fields.Example: তিনিtini/t̪ini/he, she

fields.Name: থ
fields.Example: থাকাthaka/t̪ʰa.ka/to live, to reside

fields.Name: দ
fields.Example: দেওয়াdeoẇa/d̪æo̯ɑ/to give

fields.Name: ধ
fields.Sound: dhô /d̪ʱɔ/dʱ · redhead (dental), Indian that
fields.Example: ধরাdhora/dʱɔ.ra/to hold

fields.Name: ন
fields.Example: নাna/na/no, not

fields.Name: প
fields.Example: পারাpara/paɾa/can; to be able

fields.Name: ফ
fields.Sound: phô /pʰɔ/pʰ · pinɸ (marginal consonant) · find
fields.Says: Although ফ represents the aspirated form of the voiceless bilabial stop /pʰɔ/ it is pronounced either voiceless labial fricative /ɸɔ/ (in Eastern dialects) or voiceless labiodental fricative /fɔ/ in ordinary speech.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: ফেলাphela/fæla/to drop, to let fall

fields.Name: ব
fields.Example: বলাbola/bɔla/to speak, say, state, tell

fields.Name: ভ
fields.Sound: bhô /bʱɔ/bʱ · clubhouseβ (marginal consonant) · very
fields.Says: Although ভ represents the aspirated form of the voiced bilabial stop /bʱɔ/ it is pronounced either voiced labial fricative /βɔ/ (in Eastern dialects) or voiced labiodental fricative /vɔ/ in ordinary speech.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: ভাইbhai/bʱai̯/brother

fields.Name: ম
fields.Example: মাফmaph/maf/forgiveness, pardon

fields.Name: য
fields.Sound: yô /dʒɔ~dzɔ~zɔ/d͡ʒ · hedgez (marginal consonant) · zip
fields.Says: […] whose onset was originally pronounced as a glide /j/ but became an affricate /dʒ/ in modern Bengali. It is found almost entirely at the beginning of words.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: যাওয়াjaōẇa/d͡ʒao̯a/to go

fields.Name: র
fields.Sound: rô /ɾɔ/r · American atom or ring (tapped or trilled)
fields.Says: The phonetic realisation of /r/ is usually an alveolar tap [ɾ] but can also be an alveolar approximant [ɹ] or, very rarely, an alveolar trill [r] depending on the variety and speaker.Wikipedia, Help:IPA/Bengali
fields.Example: রাখাrakha/rakʰa/to put, to place, to lay

fields.Name: ল
fields.Example: লাগাlaga[ˈlä.ɡä]to feel

fields.Name: শ
fields.Example: শুধুśudhu/ʃud̪ʱu/simply, merely, just, only

fields.Name: ষ
fields.Example: ষোলোśōlō/ʃolo/sixteen

fields.Name: স
fields.Sound: sô /sɔ~ɕɔ~ʃɔ/s · sueʃ · shoe
fields.Example: সালামsalam/salam/(chiefly Islam) hello, greetings!

fields.Name: হ
fields.Sound: hô /ɦɔ~hɔ/ɦ · behindh · head
fields.Says: When used at the beginning or end of a word, হ is pronounced voiceless /hɔ/ but when used in the middle, it is sounded voiced as /ɦɔ/.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: হওয়াhoōẇa/hɔo̯a/to be, to become; to come into existence

fields.Letter: ক খ · গ ঘ · চ ছ · জ ঝ · প ফ · ব ভ
fields.Title: অল্পপ্রাণ (Unaspirated) · মহাপ্রাণ (Aspirated)
fields.Says:
ক k scan · খ kʰ can
গ ɡ agate · ঘ ɡʱ loghouse
চ t͡ʃ catch · ছ t͡ʃʰ choose
জ d͡ʒ hedge · ঝ d͡ʒʱ hedgehog
ট ʈ American part · ঠ ʈʰ American partake
ড ɖ American bird · ঢ ɖʱ American birdhouse
ত t get (dental), Indian think · থ tʰ tub (dental), Indian thought
দ d deal (dental), Indian the · ধ dʱ redhead (dental), Indian that
প p span · ফ pʰ pin
ব b abash · ভ bʱ clubhouse
Wikipedia, Help:IPA/Bengali, the 'English approximation' of each row

fields.Letter: ত থ দ ধ · ট ঠ ড ঢ
fields.Title: Two kinds of t and d
fields.Says: Bengali contrasts dental [t] and [d] with apical postalveolar [ʈ] and [ɖ] (as well as aspirated variants). Both sets sound like /t/ and /d/ to most English speakers although the dental [t] and [d] are used in place of the English /θ/ and /ð/ for some speakers with th-stopping.Wikipedia, Help:IPA/Bengali
fields.Example:
স্বাগতśagoto/ʃaɡɔt̪o/auspicious coming or arrival, welcome
আটaṭ/aʈ/eight
দেখাdêkha/ˈd̪ɛkʰa/to see
ডাক্তারḑaktar/ɖakt̪aɾ/doctor, physician

fields.Title: Three letters, one sound
fields.Says: The voiceless palato-alveolar sibilant phoneme /ʃ/ can be written as শ (তালব্য শ talôbyô śô 'palatal śô'), ষ (মূর্ধন্য ষ murdhônyô ṣô 'retroflex ṣô') or স (দন্ত্য স dôntyô sô 'dental sô'). These graphemes once represented the alveolo-palatal /ɕ/, the retroflex /ʂ/, and the alveolar /s/ in Sanskrit, respectively, but have all merged into the palato-alveolar /ʃ/ (or /ɕ/, depending on dialect) in modern standard Bengali.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
দশdoś/d̪ɔʃ/ten
শেষśeś/ʃeʃ/conclusion, finish, end
আসাaśa/aʃa/to come

fields.Title: Two letters, one sound
fields.Says: The voiced palato-alveolar affricate /dʒ/ can be written in two ways: as য (অন্তঃস্থ য ôntôḥsthô yô 'semivocalic yô') or as জ (বর্গীয় জ bôrgiẏô jô 'plosive jô').Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
জন্যjonno/d͡ʒonːo/for; due to; because of
যেje/d͡ʒe/who, which, that (relative)

fields.Title: Two letters for n
fields.Says: […] since the consonant phoneme /n/ is written as both ন and ণ, the letters are not called simply nô; instead, they are called দন্ত্য ন dôntyô nô ('dental nô') and মূর্ধন্য ণ murdhônyô nô ('retroflex nô'). What was once pronounced and written as a retroflex nasal ণ /ɳ/ is now pronounced as an alveolar /n/ (unless conjoined with another retroflex consonant such as ট, ঠ, ড and ঢ).Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example:
নামnam/nam/name
দারুণdarun/d̪aɾun/amazing, fascinating, fabulous; cool

fields.Name: ড়
fields.Sound: ṛô /ɽɔ/ɽ · American larder
fields.Says: […] ড় and ঢ় were introduced to the inventory during the Vidyasagarian reform to indicate the retroflex flap in the pronunciation of ড ḍô and ঢ ḍhô in the middle or end of a word. It is an allophonic development in some Indic languages not present in Sanskrit. In ordinary speech these letters are pronounced the same as র in modern Bengali.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: ছাড়াchaṛa/t͡ʃʰaɽa/without

fields.Name: ঢ়
fields.Sound: ṛhô /ɽʱɔ~ɽ/ɽ · American larder
fields.Example: দৃঢ়dɾiṛho/d̪ɾiɽʱo/durable, strong

fields.Name: য়
fields.Sound: ẏô /jɔ~e̯ɔ/e̯ (semivowel) · Similar to veryj (marginal consonant) · yes
fields.Says:
The semivowel য় ẏô /e̯ɔ/ cannot occur at the beginning of a word.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
The pronunciation of য় ẏô /e̯ɔ/ varies between the glides /w/ and /j/.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: নেওয়াneōẇa/næo̯ɑ/to take

fields.Title: The line the letters hang from
fields.Says: […] the Bengali letter-forms instead hang from a visible horizontal left-to-right headstroke called মাত্রা matra. The presence and absence of this matra can be important. For example, the letter ত tô and the numeral ৩ (3) are distinguishable only by the presence or absence of the matra, as is the case between the consonant cluster ত্র trô and the independent vowel এ e.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet

fields.Name: ক্ষ
fields.Says: Certain combinations must be memorised: ক্ষ (ক+ষ) kṣô […]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: অপেক্ষাopekkha/ɔpekʰːa/wait

fields.Name: জ্ঞ
fields.Says:
[…] জ্ঞ jñô, which is a combination of জ jô and ঞ ñô, is pronounced ggô /gːɔ/ in modern Bengali […]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
As the first member of a conjunct, জ jô can lose its final down-stroke, e.g., জ্জ jjô, জ্ঞ jñô, জ্ব jbô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
As the last member of a conjunct, ঞ ñô can lose its left half (the এ part), e.g., জ্ঞ jñô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: জিজ্ঞাসাjijnaśa/d͡ʒiɡːaʃa/question

fields.Name: য-ফলা
fields.Says:
Diacritic. Used with two types of pronunciation in modern Bengali depending on the location of the consonant it is used with within a syllable E.g., when the consonant it is used with is syllable-initial, it acts as the vowel /æ/, and thus, ত্যাগ is pronounced /t̪æɡ/ E.g., when the consonant with which it is used l is syllable-final, it doubles the consonant, and thus, মুখ্য is pronounced /ˈmukʰːɔ/ […]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
When present in the middle of words, in conjuncts, য is represented as a distinct letter: ্য (যফলা yôphôla), which is mostly silent or semi-silent. The yôphôla may either alter the pronunciation of the surrounding vowel, genimate the preceding consonant, or be completely silent.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: মধ্যেmoddhe/mɔd̪ʱːe/between

fields.Name: র-ফলা
fields.Sound: রফলা rôphôla r /r/r · American atom or ring (tapped or trilled)
fields.Says: Diacritic. [r] pronounced following a consonant phoneme.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: স্ত্রীstri/st̪ɾi/woman, female

fields.Name: ব-ফলা
fields.Says: Diacritic. Used in spellings only, if they were adopted from Sanskrit and has two different pronunciations depending on the location of the consonant with which it is used. E.g., when the consonant with which it is used is syllable-initial, it remains silent, and thus, স্বাধীন is pronounced /ˈʃad̪ʱin/ (and not /*ˈʃbad̪ʱin/ or *ˈʃʋad̪ʱin/). E.g., when the consonant with which it is used is syllable-final, it doubles the consonant, and thus, বিদ্বান is pronounced /ˈbid̪ːan/ and বিশ্ব is pronounced /ˈbiʃːɔ/. […]Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: স্বামীśami/ʃami/husband

fields.Name: রেফ
fields.Sound: রেফ reph r /r/r · American atom or ring (tapped or trilled)
fields.Says: Diacritic. [ɾ] pronounced preceding a consonant phoneme.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: পর্যন্তporjonto/pɔɾd͡ʒɔnt̪o/till, until

fields.Title: Consonants written as one
fields.Says:
Clusters of up to four consonants can be orthographically represented as a typographic ligature, called a consonant conjunct (যুক্তাক্ষর/যুক্তবর্ণ yuktakṣôr/yuktôbôrṇô, or more precisely, যুক্তব্যঞ্জন yuktôbêñjôn). Typically, the first consonant in the conjunct is shown above or to the left of the following consonants. Many consonants appear in an abbreviated or compressed form when serving as part of a conjunct. Others simply take exceptional forms in conjuncts, bearing little or no resemblance to the base character.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
Often, consonant conjuncts are not actually pronounced as would be implied by the pronunciation of the individual components. For example, adding ল lô underneath শ śô in Bengali creates the conjunct শ্ল, which is pronounced /slɔ/ (and not /ʃlɔ/) in Bengali.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet

fields.Name: ন্ত
fields.Example: কিন্তুkintu/kint̪u/but

fields.Name: ষ্ট
fields.Says: As the first member of a conjunct, ষ ṣô is compressed and simplified to an oval shape with a diagonal stroke through it. It is placed to the top-left of the following consonants, e.g., ষ্ক ṣkô, ষ্ট ṣṭô, ষ্ঠ ṣṭhô, ষ্প ṣpô, ষ্ফ ṣphô, ষ্ম ṣmô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: চেষ্টাceśṭa/t͡ʃeʃʈa/attempt, endeavour, effort, enterprise

fields.Name: স্ত
fields.Says: As the first member of a conjunct, স sô is compressed and simplified to a ribbon shape. It is placed above or to the top-left of the following consonant, e.g., স্ক skô, স্খ skhô, স্ত stô, স্থ sthô, স্ন snô, স্প spô, স্ফ sphô, স্ব sbô, স্ম smô, স্ল slô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: রাস্তাrasta/rast̪a/road, street

fields.Name: ক্ত
fields.Says: When followed by র rô or ত tô, ক kô takes on the same form as ত tô would with the addition of a curl to the right, e.g., ক্র krô, ক্ত ktô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: রক্তrokto/ˈrɔk.t̪o/blood

fields.Name: স্থ
fields.Says:
As the first member of a conjunct, স sô is compressed and simplified to a ribbon shape. It is placed above or to the top-left of the following consonant, e.g., স্ক skô, স্খ skhô, স্ত stô, স্থ sthô, স্ন snô, স্প spô, স্ফ sphô, স্ব sbô, স্ম smô, স্ল slô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
As the last member of a conjunct, থ thô can lose its final upstroke, taking the form of হ hô instead, e.g., ন্থ nthô স্থ, sthô, ম্থ mthô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: অবস্থাobostha/ɔbost̪ʰa/state, condition, situation, circumstances

fields.Name: ঙ্গ
fields.Says: As the first member of a conjunct, ঙ ṅô can appear as a loop and curl, e.g., ঙ্ক ṅkô, ঙ্গ ṅgô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: সঙ্গেśoṅge/ʃɔŋɡe/with; in the company of

fields.Name: চ্ছ
fields.Says: As the first member of a conjunct, the consonants ঙ ṅô, চ cô, ড ḍô, and ব bô are often compressed and placed at the top-left of the following consonant with little or no change to the basic shape, e.g., ঙ্ক্ষ ṅkṣô, ঙ্খ ṅkhô, ঙ্ঘ ṅghô, ঙ্ম ṅmô, চ্চ ccô, চ্ছ cchô, চ্ঞ cñô, ড্ঢ ḍḍhô, ব্ব bbô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: শুভেচ্ছাśubheccha/ʃubʱet͡ʃʰːa/well-wish

fields.Name: দ্ধ
fields.Says: As the last member of a conjunct, the curled top of ধ dhô is replaced by a straight downstroke to the right, taking the form of ঝ jhô instead, e.g., গ্ধ gdhô, দ্ধ ddhô, ন্ধ ndhô, ব্ধ bdhô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: যুদ্ধjuddho/d͡ʒud̪ʱːo/war

fields.Name: ন্দ
fields.Says: The consonants can also be placed side-by-side, sharing their vertical line, e.g., দ্দ ddô, ন্দ ndô, ব্দ bdô, ব্জ bjô প্ট, pṭô, স্ট sṭô, শ্চ ścô, শ্ছ śchô, etc.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: পছন্দpochondo/pɔt͡ʃʰond̪o/preference

fields.Name: ন্ধ
fields.Says: As the last member of a conjunct, the curled top of ধ dhô is replaced by a straight downstroke to the right, taking the form of ঝ jhô instead, e.g., গ্ধ gdhô, দ্ধ ddhô, ন্ধ ndhô, ব্ধ bdhô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: বন্ধুbondhu/bond̪ʱu/friend

fields.Name: স্ক
fields.Says: As the first member of a conjunct, স sô is compressed and simplified to a ribbon shape. It is placed above or to the top-left of the following consonant, e.g., স্ক skô, স্খ skhô, স্ত stô, স্থ sthô, স্ন snô, স্প spô, স্ফ sphô, স্ব sbô, স্ম smô, স্ল slô.Wikipedia, Bengali alphabet
fields.Example: স্কুলskul/skul/school, academy

fields.Name: স্ত্র
fields.Example: অস্ত্রostro/ɔst̪ɾo/weapon
